title: Retainer after braces
what: A retainer holds your teeth in place after braces. It can be fixed, a thin wire behind the teeth, or a removable clear tray.
why: After braces or aligners are removed, so the teeth do not move back to their old position.
duration: placement usually takes 20 to 40 minutes; you usually wear it for years, and the orthodontist will tell you how long
tell_doctor: If a retainer has broken or come loose before

prepare.title: Teeth
prepare.text: Brush your teeth before the visit.

prepare.title: Timing
prepare.text: If your braces are being removed, the retainer is often placed the same day.

bring: The tray case, if you already have one
steps: Your teeth are cleaned and dried
For a fixed retainer, the wire is bonded to the inside of the teeth
For a removable one, an impression is taken and the tray is given later
Shows you how to care for it and how to wear the tray
feel: For the first days you can feel the wire with your tongue
The tray feels tight at first. This passes quickly
after: Wear the tray as many hours as the doctor said, usually at night
Clean around the wire with a small brush or floss
Keep the tray in its case
Come to check-ups at the set time
red_flags: The wire has come off or broken: book a visit with the doctor, do not wait
The tray cracked or no longer fits

faq.q: How long do I wear a retainer?
faq.a: Usually a long time, sometimes for years. The orthodontist will tell you exactly.

faq.q: What happens if I don't wear it?
faq.a: Your teeth can slowly shift back.

reminders.text: Orthodontist visit tomorrow. Brush your teeth and bring your tray case if you have one.
